name: SQL Injection
description: Untrusted input concatenated into SQL queries. Indicators: '+' or f-strings in query strings, raw execute() calls. Flask/Django context: db.session.execute(query), cursor.execute(query).
remediation: Use parameterized queries, SQLAlchemy ORM, or Django QuerySet. Never use string interpolation for database calls.

name: Cross-Site Scripting (XSS)
description: Untrusted input rendered in UI without proper escaping. Indicators: render_template_string(), SafeString(), |safe filter in Jinja2, or returning raw HTML strings in Flask.
remediation: Use Jinja2 auto-escaping (default in render_template). Avoid |safe and render_template_string with user input. Use Flask-Talisman for CSP.

name: Server-Side Template Injection (SSTI)
description: User input processed by template engine. Indicators: render_template_string() in Flask where input contains {{ }}. Attacker can execute arbitrary code via template context.
remediation: Never pass user input directly to render_template_string. Use static template files (render_template) with context variables.

name: OS Command Injection
description: Executing system commands using untrusted input. Indicators: os.system(), subprocess.Popen(shell=True), subprocess.call(), or call().
remediation: Use subprocess.run() with shell=False and pass arguments as a list. Avoid os.system and shell=True.

name: Path Traversal
description: Accessing files outside intended directory using '../'. Indicators: open(), os.path.join() with untrusted input, send_from_directory() without absolute path check.
remediation: Use werkzeug.utils.secure_filename(). Validate path with os.path.abspath and check prefix.

name: Insecure Deserialization
description: Untrusted data deserialized into objects. Indicators: pickle.load(), yaml.load() (without SafeLoader), or marshal.loads().
remediation: Avoid pickle with untrusted data. Use yaml.safe_load() or JSON for data exchange.

name: Hardcoded Credentials
description: Embedding passwords, keys, or Flask SECRET_KEY in source code. Indicators: app.config['SECRET_KEY'] = 'fixed_string', passwords in code.
remediation: Use environment variables or a manager. Rotate keys regularly.

name: Information Exposure via Debug Mode
description: Flask/Django debug mode enabled in production. Indicators: app.run(debug=True), DEBUG = True in config. Reveals stack traces and environment variables.
remediation: Set debug=False in production. Use environment-specific configuration files.

name: Cookie Without 'HttpOnly' Flag
description: Session cookies are accessible via JavaScript. Indicator: SESSION_COOKIE_HTTPONLY = False or not set in Flask config.
remediation: Set SESSION_COOKIE_HTTPONLY = True in Flask settings.

name: Cookie Without 'Secure' Flag
description: Session cookies sent over unencrypted HTTP. Indicator: SESSION_COOKIE_SECURE = False or not set in Flask config.
remediation: Set SESSION_COOKIE_SECURE = True in Flask settings and use HTTPS.

name: Session Fixation
description: Not regenerating session ID after login. Indicator: Flask login without session.clear() or session.permanent=True management.
remediation: Use Flask-Login's login_user() which handles session regeneration, or call session.clear() manually before login.

name: Broken Cryptography
description: Using weak crypto (MD5, SHA1). Indicators: hashlib.md5(), hashlib.sha1() for passwords.
remediation: Use bcrypt, Argon2, or PBKDF2 for password hashing.
